title: Shape-memory alloy fatigue life
bottleneck: Nickel-titanium shape-memory alloys recover large deformations, but repeated cycling accumulates dislocations that degrade the transformation: actuation stroke shrinks, hysteresis grows, and devices drift out of calibration within thousands of cycles instead of the millions that applications need. High-temperature shape-memory alloys for engines and actuators fatigue even faster. The microstructural origins of functional fatigue are understood only qualitatively.
why_it_blocks: Reliable shape-memory actuators could replace motors and hydraulics in aircraft, medical devices, and robotics with lighter, simpler systems. Fatigue-limited life keeps them in niche uses like stents and eyeglass frames rather than in safety-critical actuation.
current_state: Precipitation-hardened and copper-alloyed variants have pushed cycle counts higher in the lab, and some aerospace actuators are in testing. But million-cycle, drift-free performance at useful work output is still beyond reach for most compositions.
